chains.title: GATA2 at the LMO1 intronic dELS

links.claim: GATA2 is the best-supported GATA-factor candidate for this GATA motif: QBiC-SELEX shows the alt A allele binds the GATA group less strongly than ref C (effect -0.816), with GATA2 as the best-scoring own-model member and the highest-expressed GATA factor in ACH-000149 (133.07 TPM). GATA2 ChIP-seq in SK-N-SH contains the variant, supporting occupancy but not allele specificity. The literature reports a GATA/TATA motif in the LMO1 first intron; on the LMO1 minus strand, plus-strand ref C corresponds to G and alt A to T. This is a binding prediction plus occupancy, not direct allele-specific GATA2 binding.
The variant lies within distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1518342 (dELS), with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 signal in ENCODE/SCREEN, making it a plausible regulatory element.
This element is assigned to LMO1: LMO1 is the nearest protein-coding gene (34.9 kb, in gene body) and is the best L2G gene across credible sets.

The relevant cell context is neuroblastoma, specifically the adrenergic state: the case expression context is ACH-000149/SK-N-SH, GATA2 ChIP-seq occupies the variant in SK-N-SH, and the literature links the LMO1 intronic GATA/TATA switch to adrenergic neuroblastoma initiation.

The ref C/GATA allele is expected to preserve GATA-driven LMO1 enhancer activity and adrenergic-state initiation, while the alt A/TATA allele reduces it and lowers initiation risk. E06f/E06g support a GATA/TATA switch affecting neuroblastoma initiation, and E20 provides an allele-specific eQTL in skeletal muscle with alt A associated with lower LMO1 expression, consistent in direction but not neuroblastoma-specific. GATA2-specific causation is not established by these data.

predictions: Allele-specific GATA2 EMSA or GATA2 ChIP shows stronger GATA2 binding on ref C than alt A at rs2168101.
Reporter or MPRA assays in SK-N-SH show higher enhancer activity for ref C than alt A.
LMO1 expression is higher with ref C than alt A in adrenergic neuroblastoma cells, consistent with the E20 eQTL direction.
GATA2 perturbation reduces LMO1 and/or adrenergic-state markers in the relevant cell context.
falsified_if: Allele-specific EMSA, GATA2 ChIP, or reporter assays show no ref-vs-alt difference in GATA2 binding at rs2168101.
The alt A allele increases rather than decreases LMO1 enhancer activity or LMO1 expression in SK-N-SH or adrenergic neuroblastoma cells.
GATA2 perturbation does not reduce LMO1 or adrenergic-state markers in the relevant cell context.

chains.title: GATA3 alternative GATA-factor chain

links.claim: GATA3 is a plausible alternative GATA factor: it is an own-model passing member of the GATA QBiC-SELEX group with alt A binding less than ref C (z -54.11), it is expressed in ACH-000149 at 51.82 TPM (lower than GATA2), and GATA3 ChIP-seq in SK-N-SH contains the variant. This supports occupancy but not allele-specific GATA3 binding; GATA2 is favored by higher expression and ChIP, so this is a secondary GATA-factor chain.
The variant lies in distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1518342 with ENCODE/SCREEN enhancer marks.
The element is linked to LMO1 by proximity and by L2G scoring.

The relevant disease cell context is neuroblastoma; SK-N-SH is the provided expression context, GATA3 ChIP-seq occupies the variant in SK-N-SH, and the literature connects the LMO1 regulatory GATA/TATA switch to adrenergic neuroblastoma.

If GATA3 rather than GATA2 mediates the effect, the same GATA/TATA direction is expected: ref C preserves GATA-driven LMO1 expression and adrenergic phenotype, while alt A lowers it and reduces initiation risk. E06f/E06g support the motif-switch direction, and E20 provides a directionally consistent allele-specific LMO1 eQTL, but no data establish GATA3 specificity.

predictions: Allele-specific GATA3 ChIP or EMSA shows stronger GATA3 binding on ref C than alt A at EH38E1518342.
GATA3 knockdown reduces LMO1 in SK-N-SH.
GATA3 binding, more than GATA2 binding, tracks allele-specific enhancer activity at rs2168101.
falsified_if: GATA3 is not expressed or not bound at this cCRE in SK-N-SH.
GATA3 knockdown has no effect on LMO1 expression or enhancer activity.
Allele-specific GATA binding at rs2168101 is fully explained by GATA2 and not GATA3.

grades_v0.reason: TF-specific allele effect is not directly shown; QBiC-SELEX GATA group is only an in vitro binding prediction and the literature GATA-motif evidence does not name GATA2.
E03 directly places the variant in dELS EH38E1518342 with DNase/H3K27ac/H3K4me3 marks.
E02 places LMO1 34.9 kb away in gene body and E05 gives LMO1 as the best L2G gene; this supports LMO1 as the target assignment.
E06g links the LMO1 regulatory GATA/TATA switch to adrenergic neuroblastoma initiation, and E07 supplies the ACH-000149 expression context.

E06f/E06g support a GATA/TATA switch affecting neuroblastoma initiation, but they do not demonstrate GATA2-dependent LMO1 expression or the claimed direction of LMO1 expression. The alt-protective direction is consistent with E06g.
GATA3 is a passing own_model GATA-group member, but no GATA3-specific ChIP, allele-specific assay, or reporter evidence is shown; QBiC-SELEX alone is only weak binding support.
E03 directly supports the dELS element.
E02 proximity and E05 L2G support LMO1 as the linked gene.
The neuroblastoma/adrenergic context is supported by the case context and E06g, although not specifically for GATA3.
The generic GATA/TATA switch phenotype is supported, but there is no evidence that GATA3 is the relevant GATA factor; this link is conditional and indirect.
DBP has an own_model QBiC-SELEX prediction with alt binding more, but this is a binding prediction only; no DBP ChIP, allele-specific assay, or reporter evidence is shown.
E03 directly supports the dELS element.
E02 proximity and E05 L2G support LMO1 as the linked gene.
The ACH-000149/SK-N-SH context and DBP TPM are provided, but there is no evidence DBP acts in this regulatory element or cell state.

E06a/E06b concern LMO1 overexpression and pro-metastatic macrophage reprogramming, not DBP, rs2168101, or alt-allele enhancer activity. The claim that alt A increases LMO1 via DBP is not supported and is directionally at odds with the protective alt/TATA initiation evidence in E06g.
